Byproduct

/BY-prod-uhkt/ - the stress falls on BY · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Byproduct means something produced incidentally while something else is being made.

Candied peel began as a byproduct: rind left over from pressing oranges for juice, too fragrant for anyone to throw away.

Worked Example

The data center on the ring road exists to run computations, and it is very good at the one thing computation always does on the side: it gets hot. For years, fans pushed that warmth into the sky. Then the town ran a pipe. The server halls now heat the public swimming pool through the winter, and the manager likes to say the town swims in arithmetic.

Byproduct is the exact word for that warmth, because it names something produced incidentally while something else is being made. Nobody built the halls to warm a pool — the heat simply falls out of the real work — and finding a use for it is what turns an incidental output from a nuisance into an asset.

How Byproduct Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

side effect

side effect: the unplanned result of an action, good or bad; a byproduct is the unplanned thing a process makes

spin-off

spin-off: a byproduct that has grown into its own venture

Antonyms

centerpiece

centerpiece: the intended star of the whole effort

end product

end product: the output the process exists to deliver

How Strong Is It? — product → byproduct → waste

product vs. byproduct

product vs. byproduct: The product is the whole point of the process — the thing everyone came to make; it sits at the intended end of this scale.

waste vs. byproduct

waste vs. byproduct: Waste lies further from the point than a byproduct — a byproduct at least finds a buyer or a use; waste is the output nobody wants at any price.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — by-

Prefix — by-: beside, on the side (as in bystander, byway)

Root — product

Root — product: thing brought forth (Latin producere, to lead forth)

Put it together

Put it together: By- (beside, on the side) + product (thing brought forth) = the thing brought forth on the side. English built this one at home: the same by- that gives us a bystander — someone standing off to the side of the action — marks the product standing off to the side of the real work.

Use the root in a new word: aqueduct

Use the root in a new word: aqueduct: Product rests on Latin duc-, "to lead"; an aqueduct joins it to aqua and literally leads water across a valley.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Byproduct is the accountant's honest word for the thing you made without meaning to — whey, stone dust, waste heat. Use side effect when the incidental result is an event or condition rather than a thing, and spin-off when the sideline has grown a life of its own. The word carries no judgment: a byproduct can be worth nothing or worth more than the product itself.
